abstract: We compute local residue selectors for generalized Thomas sections. Under contact normalization, the Hessian-null derivative must be supplemented by a zero-order term determined by the transformed volume density and the contact unit. An explicit cubic gives a nonzero correction even for a constant numerator. A section with two $D_4$ singularities integrates this local calculation with a defect-two relation space and detects a specified integral algebraic class through its Saito pairing. Five standalone exact Singular programs and retained outputs support these finite models; the residue matrices are tied to the mathematical derivation. The remaining material provides controlled examples and scope restrictions. A plane-containing cubic fourfold supplies a complete nodal control for the primitive plane class. A specialization of the published rational-root and join construction for fake linear cycles gives an annihilator whose associated hyperplane section is smooth. This refutes only the explicit unrestricted per-member implication from a linear annihilator to singular support, and does not exclude a different detecting member in the same net. No novelty is claimed for fake linear cycles, the complete-intersection period formulas or the general defect machinery. An appendix separates the quadratic-polarization transfer criterion from a mere weight-two Hodge map and records the known Weil-support construction with an additional local-freeness hypothesis. Reflexivity alone does not establish that hypothesis. The results prove no new general case of the Hodge conjecture.
author: lihongmin
change_summary:
1. Section 1 (contribution paragraph), per the v2 review: the two examples are now stated separately; the nonzero contact-density correction is attributed to the explicit cubic, and it is stated that the correction vanishes at both singularities of the two-D4 detecting section, which therefore illustrates the selector framework and detection rather than detection requiring a nonzero correction.
2. Section 5: the two-D4 section is introduced as a second, independent example, and a sentence after the residue pairings records that its density correction is zero at both points and that the nonzero correction is exhibited only by the preceding cubic.
3. Section 6: the limitations paragraph notes that the density term is nonzero in the first cubic and vanishes in the two-D4 detecting section. No mathematical content, computation or supplement changed.
4. Section 5 (density example): the D4 residue block now includes the density term; the full matrix with the four nodal evaluation rows is displayed, with rank four and kernel C(2Z+X), versus kernel CZ if the correction is omitted. The supplement matrix, which had omitted the term, is corrected and now checks the kernel; the singular set is closed by the gradient equations.
5. Theorem 5.1: the weight-two projection is justified by the weighted Euler field, d(i_E alpha_k)=(k-2)alpha_k.
6. Section 2: the relation space, Tate twist, eigenvalue-one part and (0,0) part are defined for sections with isolated singularities. Section 3: the four-node claim is closed by the projective Jacobian length four. Section 4: delta and the polynomial-ring versus Jacobian-ring annihilators are defined explicitly.
7. Appendix A.1.3: the boxed conclusion now yields a Hodge class in general and a Hodge-Weil class only for the model of [10]; K(B) is defined, the tangent bundle is written separately from the transcendental structure, and the pullback is stated through j^*. Reproducibility: coefficient fields and the Jacobian-cone label are corrected.
8. Sections 3 and 5: Saito's criterion is cited as [2, Theorem 1(ii)] (the pairing criterion for generalized Thomas sections), checked against arXiv:0806.1461.
9. Sections 3 and 4: the period-annihilator ideal is cited as [7, Definition 2.1] with the Jacobian-ideal containment [7, Lemma 2.3] (checked against arXiv:1908.03221); its identification with the colon ideal (J_F:P_delta) is stated as a consequence of the period polynomial [6] and Gorenstein duality rather than attributed to [7]. No mathematical content or supplement changed.
10. Sections 2, 3 and Appendix A (independently checked against the arXiv originals): nodal vanishing cohomology Q(-n) with unipotent monodromy cited as [2, Theorem 3]; the linear part of the plane annihilator noted to agree with [7, Corollary 2.7 and Example 2.8]; the Weil-class statement cited as [10, Theorem 0.2] and [10, Proposition 1.11].
title: Generalized Thomas Sections and Density-Corrected Residue Selectors
